newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - European shares advance, dollar weaker.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - European shares advance, dollar weaker.

text.p: European shares made further progress in early trading on Thursday, helped by higher bond prices, with the London stock market, Europe's busiest, up nearly half a percent.
On the currency market the dollar was weaker, having slipped overnight. But analysts said it was neither likely to make up much ground in pre-Easter holiday trading nor drop much further.
London share traders expected pre-holiday caution amid uncertainty over higher interest rates and the British election campaign. The market will be closed on Friday and Monday.
"A lot of people will be starting their holiday early and those who are at their desks today will probably just watch their screens," the head of trading at a major London brokerage said.
Traders still at work are already fretting about the next tightening of American monetary policy after this week's quarter percentage point interest rate rise.
Analysts speculate that the Federal Reserve could boost U.S. rates again in May to keep a lid on inflation.
Meanwhile, the diary has little in the way of corporate news or economic data to whip up enthusiasm.
The key FTSE-100 index of British blue-chip share prices has gained around 86 points or two percent over the past two sessions but Wall Street gave little new lead overnight.

"The Dow is still looking vulnerable. The Street was hoping that the Fed rate hike would be the last for awhile but now people are talking about another quarter-point hike in May," one London dealer said.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 4.53 points to 6,880.70 on Wednesday, while the technology-laden Nasdaq Composite index jumped 21.02 points to 1,269.08.
In Frankfurt, shares were led higher by car companies, partly catching up with gains in later electronic trade on Wednesday, but some profit-taking was seen ahead of the holiday.
Stronger bond markets and the marginal gain on Wall Street also helped French shares revive after opening marginally weaker, with healthy company results giving support.
But Paris traders said trading was likely to be affected by the expiry during the day of March futures and options.

For the dollar, meanwhile, concern over Japan's large trade surplus and disappointment that it failed to gain more after Tuesday's rate rise were depressants. But underlying sentiment is still good and it is unlikely to drop much, analysts said.
The U.S. currency slipped against the yen in Asian business after concern expressed by U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers about Japan's trade surplus with the United States.
"The dollar's slipped a bit on the Summers comment but it's very quiet in Europe with the holidays beckoning," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered.
Summers said Washington had frequently expressed concern about the "dangerous possibility" that the Japanese current account surplus would expand substantially.
Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin will visit Japan on April 4 for talks in which the nagging trade tensions are expected to feature prominently.
On the data front, U.S. weekly jobless claims at 1330 GMT provide the main interest, followed by U.S. February home sales at 1500 GMT.
CURRENCIES AT 1000 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.6828 marks and 123.71 yen, compared with 1.6920 and 124.16 in late European trading on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1015 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 18.7 points or 0.43 percent, at 4,320.2.
PARIS - The CAC-40 index was 17.63 points or 0.67 percent ahead at 2,666.36.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 14.69 points, or 0.43 percent, at 3,432.81.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was quoted around $349.70 an ounce, up from the previous London close of $348.75 in quiet trading. Silver was steady at $5.15.
